home.lazyvim_tmux_and_docker_are_included_cur: LazyVim, tmux and Docker are included. Curated installs add editors, language toolchains and AI coding agents, while Git identities and cloud menus keep account context explicit.
home.steam_comes_installed_with_gamemode_mang: Steam comes installed with GameMode, MangoHud, gamescope and 32-bit graphics drivers. Game Mode turns off animations, blur and notification popups while you play.
home.on_supported_snapshot_setups_system_upda: On supported snapshot setups, System Update checks Arch news and takes a Btrfs snapshot before an upgrade. Recovery has documented layout and boot requirements; keep an independent backup too.
home.yes_free_to_download_use_and_share_with_: Yes, free to download, use and share, with no account, subscription or paid tier. Eitr is open source: its code is GPL-3.0 and its artwork CC BY 4.0, all developed in the open on GitHub. If it makes your days better, you can sponsor its development.
home.about_two_minutes_in_a_virtual_machine_o: About two minutes in a virtual machine on a fast computer, from confirming to finished. Everything comes from the ISO, so nothing is downloaded while it installs.

home.no_the_iso_carries_the_packages_needed_f: No. The ISO carries the packages needed for guided offline installation. Later updates and optional tool downloads need a connection; optional services also keep their own account requirements.
home.can_i_break_it_with_an_update: Can I break it with an update?
home.on_supported_layouts_system_update_takes: On supported layouts, System Update takes a Btrfs snapshot before an upgrade. Recovery has documented layout and boot requirements, and snapshots do not replace an independent backup. Read the recovery Handbook chapter before relying on a rollback.
home.eitr_does_not_require_an_eitr_online_acc: Eitr does not require an Eitr online account or collect usage telemetry. Weather, updates and optional connected tools talk to their own services. Problem reports are prepared for your review and sent only when you choose.
home.an_arch_based_linux_distribution_from_th: An Arch-based Linux distribution from the far north
home.a_keyboard_first_arch_linux_distribution: A keyboard-first Arch Linux distribution built around Hyprland and Quickshell, with its own ISO, guided offline installer and signed package repository alongside Arch’s. Your desktop, development tools, cloud accounts and system management in one coherent system; graphical controls are there when you want them, never required.
home.eitr_is_the_default_theme_every_theme_re: Eitr is the default theme. Every theme recolors the bar, terminal, launcher, lockscreen, editors and apps; Eitr and each realm have their own Neovim and VS Code colors. Each comes with its own wallpapers.
home.download_the_iso_check_it_write_it_to_a_: Download the ISO, check it, write it to a USB stick, boot it and follow the installer: about two minutes on a fast machine, with nothing to download. It can erase a disk or install beside Windows (installing beside Windows is so far tested only in a VM). Everything on
home.each_release_takes_its_name_from_the_old: Each release takes its name from the old stories, from the first being to the bridge between worlds.
home.a_preview_for_early_users_the_installer_: A preview for early users. The installer, updates and recovery pass automated VM tests and run on the first real machine; other hardware is what we learn from you. Something broke? Settings > System > Information > Report a Problem.
home.eitr_is_free_and_open_source_made_in_the: EITR is free and open source, made in the open and tested on every release. If it makes your days at the computer better, you can support its development with a one-time or monthly sponsorship.

about.eitr_linux_is_an_arch_based_linux_distri: Eitr Linux is an Arch-based Linux distribution built around Hyprland and a custom Quickshell desktop. Its own ISO and guided installer bring you to a complete keyboard-first environment, with Eitr packages delivered through a signed repository alongside Arch’s.
about.hyprland_arranges_windows_and_workspaces: Hyprland arranges windows and workspaces. Eitr’s Quickshell bar, notifications, native panels and Control Center share the same visual language. Walker and Elephant bring applications, settings and actions into one searchable menu system.
about.use_shortcuts_when_you_want_to_move_quic: Use shortcuts when you want to move quickly, or open graphical controls for sound, networking, displays and appearance. A theme reaches the bar, launcher, terminal, lockscreen and supported applications, rather than stopping at the wallpaper.
about.eitr_is_for_people_who_want_arch_s_packa: Eitr is for people who want Arch’s packages and a keyboard-first desktop without assembling every panel and everyday workflow themselves. Developer environments, cloud accounts, Git identities and coding assistants are available through its menus. Gaming, capture tools and offline dictation are part of the same desktop.
about.you_can_inspect_the_configuration_and_so: You can inspect the configuration and source, choose your tools and change the defaults. Optional assistants keep their own sign-in and permission boundaries; using Eitr does not require an AI subscription.
about.eitr_uses_arch_linux_and_pacman_with_its: Eitr uses Arch Linux and pacman, with its own desktop packages, installer, artwork and integration. System Update combines Arch updates with the signed [eitr] repository and, on supported snapshot setups, checks for changes before creating a Btrfs snapshot. From a terminal,
about.update_without_automatic_snapshots_the_o: update without automatic snapshots. The offline Handbook documents the desktop and its recovery procedures.
about.eitr_s_code_is_free_and_open_source_unde: Eitr’s code is free and open source under GPL-3.0-or-later. Its artwork is CC BY 4.0; third-party components retain their own licenses.
about.eitr_runs_daily_on_its_developer_s_deskt: Eitr runs daily on its developer’s desktop. Released ISOs pass automated VM checks for offline installation, updates and factory resets. That is evidence for those configurations, not a promise that every laptop, graphics card or recovery scenario has been tested.
about.the_beta_label_describes_validation_and_: The beta label describes validation and support scope; it does not remove the desktop or development workflows described here. Read the current hardware and recovery limitations before installing. Independent testing and useful problem reports help expand what Eitr can verify.

features.eitr_linux_brings_an_arch_based_system_a: Eitr Linux brings an Arch-based system, a native Hyprland desktop and everyday tools into one distribution. Here is what is available, what is optional, and what still needs testing.
features.the_custom_quickshell_desktop_includes_n: The custom Quickshell desktop includes native notifications, a workspace Overview with live previews, and panels for audio, WiFi, Bluetooth, displays, calendar, weather and hardware. The Eitr logo or Super + comma opens Control Center, including a disposable, read-only quick chat that knows Eitr through the Handbook. Walker searches applications, menus, settings and actions. Install > VPN offers Tailscale, WireGuard configuration import and NetworkManager VPN plugins, with reviewed imports and explicit connection choices.
features.choose_full_centered_with_evenly_packed_: Choose Full, Centered with evenly packed icons around a centered clock, or Tabs: three content-sized tabs joined by slopes on a thin strip, floating panels and weather on hover. Active workspace glyphs use the accent color; AI Usage has its own icon.
features.place_monitors_beside_one_another_choose: Place monitors beside one another, choose a main display, and show the bar on one or all screens. HDR monitors get an HDR switch with SDR content brightness.
features.adjust_per_application_audio_and_microph: Adjust per-application audio and microphone controls in one panel; choose Bars or Line for the media equalizer.
features.themes_with_matching_application_colors_: themes, with matching application colors, lockscreens, 4K wallpapers and ultrawide artwork. Eitr is the default; it and each realm have their own Neovim and VS Code colors, and setup wizards follow the current theme.
features.add_wallpapers_from_a_file_or_link_for_a: Add wallpapers from a file or link for all themes or one theme; generate a theme from a picture, edit colors live, and create your own lockscreen.
features.keep_your_preferred_bar_position_corners: Keep your preferred bar position, corners, cursor and fonts when switching themes. Auto-hide reveals the bar at its screen edge; Reduce motion makes desktop transitions instant.
features.kitty_zsh_tmux_neovim_with_lazyvim_docke: Kitty, Zsh, tmux, Neovim with LazyVim, Docker, Lazygit and Lazydocker form the development workspace. Menus offer additional editors, language environments, database clients, API tools and monitoring dashboards. Schema v2 plugins add tools, tiles, panels, desktop widgets and bar items from reviewed Git commits. Control Center’s Plugins page manages them;
features.reviews_updates_separately_from_system_u: reviews updates separately from System Update.
features.claude_code_codex_github_copilot_cli_gro: Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, Grok and Gemini CLI are available through first-use installation. Antigravity, OpenCode and Pi are also available as standalone assistants. Super + A opens your default assistant trusted in the home folder, with full access and offline Handbook guidance where supported. Settings > Security > Assistant Access restores permission prompts. Development > AI opens normal sessions in a picked folder, with account switching and session options where supported. Ratatoskr is the experimental offline assistant. The bar shows supported usage information.
features.the_optional_let_assistants_work_togethe: The optional “Let assistants work together” feature connects supported clients through a local bridge. Another signed-in assistant can give a read-only second opinion from the same working folder. Hand-offs retain the caller’s tool-approval boundary; helpers cannot delegate onward. Real-account verification remains a separate step from mock and unit tests; Gemini has answered read-only and through the bridge with a free API key; Antigravity is not a collaboration helper.
features.failed_task_terminals_offer_ask_the_ai_c: Failed task terminals offer Ask the AI; crash notifications offer assistant help or a problem report with crash details. These are opt-in workflows; Eitr does not silently send every crash to an AI service. Provider accounts, subscriptions and network access are separate from the distribution.
features.git_accounts_manages_folder_specific_ide: Git Accounts manages folder-specific identities and SSH keys. Cloud menus make provider accounts and project, subscription, region or scope selections explicit, with navigation back through account, service and resource menus.
features.system_security_users_lists_existing_hum: Settings > Security > Users lists existing human accounts as read-only rows. Create User… opens a wizard for the username, optional full name, Standard or Administrator account type and password, with a review before creation. Each new account sets up its own desktop at its first Hyprland login through UWSM, without copying files from your account. User deletion is not offered.
features.provider_menus_cover_aws_azure_google_cl: Provider menus cover AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Cloudflare, DigitalOcean, Hetzner Cloud, IBM Cloud, Netlify, Oracle Cloud and Vercel. The newer provider workflows have isolated account workspaces and mock-tested resource views; live installation, sign-in and remote context checks remain open where documented. Menu availability is not a claim that every vendor workflow has passed real-account testing.
features.an_organization_profile_is_a_json_file_o: An organization profile is a JSON file on the installer’s answers stick. It removes reviewed optional apps, adds packages, Flathub apps and checksummed package files, sets defaults such as the theme, wallpaper, browser and an extra signed repository, and applies policies: leave out groups such as gaming or media, and hide and refuse remote access, assistant collaboration and update-channel changes. Review lists every change before the disk is touched;
features.do_the_same_on_an_installed_machine: do the same on an installed machine.
features.policies_govern_eitr_s_own_tools_they_ar: Policies govern Eitr’s own tools; they are not a lockdown. A user with root can edit or override them, so real lockdown also means not granting root. Installs with and without a network, a refused profile and applying a profile to an installed machine have passed in a virtual machine. Package upgrades, hidden controls and installer screens in every language have also passed in a virtual machine.
features.read_the_profile_format_and_limits: Read the profile format and limits ↗
features.capture_screenshots_record_with_obs_read: Capture screenshots, record with OBS, read screen text or QR codes, pick a color and share nearby with LocalSend. Tap Super + D twice or hold and release for local dictation. Hold Super + Shift + D for voice reminders, or type everyday times such as “9am”, “in 5 minutes” and “every 29th”. Repeats and appointment alerts appear in the calendar; a missing time opens the native HH:MM clock with any assistant. Alerts chime unless Do Not Disturb is on, with snooze and dismiss actions in popups and notification history.
features.tools_calendars_adds_read_only_google_ou: Tools > Calendar Sources adds read-only Google, Outlook or iCal subscriptions using a secret calendar address, refreshed when you open the panel. Edit provider events at their source. The offline Handbook opens with Super + F1.
features.web_apps_open_in_their_own_window_with_a: Web apps open in their own window with a chosen browser profile. Eitr follows your compatible default browser, supports Vivaldi and offers to install Chromium when needed.
features.steam_comes_installed_with_gamemode_mang: Steam comes installed with GameMode, MangoHud and gamescope; RetroArch and GeForce NOW are optional, for classic and cloud gaming. On HDR monitors, fullscreen HDR games turn HDR on by themselves, tone-mapped to the monitor's own brightness range, and an HDR switch in the display settings shows the whole desktop in HDR. Game Mode can disable animations, blur and notification popups. Individual games, controllers and cloud services have their own compatibility and account requirements.
features.system_update_checks_arch_news_and_avail: System Update checks Arch news and available changes, creates a Btrfs snapshot when an upgrade is needed, and updates from Arch and Eitr’s signed repository, repairing stale package-list signatures when needed. Installing an app while updates are waiting explains why the system must be current first and offers to run System Update, snapshot included, then install. From a terminal,
features.update_without_automatic_snapshots_while: update without automatic snapshots. While it works, each step shows a turning rune and Bifröst-colored text, and pacman shows color and its Pac-Man progress bar.
features.system_maintenance_check_this_pc_runs_re: Settings > System > Maintenance > Check This PC runs read-only checks with suggested fixes. Optional deeper checks ask for your password; neither repairs nor restarts anything.
features.system_maintenance_choose_fastest_mirror: Settings > System > Maintenance > Choose Fastest Mirrors uses reflector to rank Arch package mirrors by download speed. Fresh installs try automatically after a boot with a network, with up to three connected attempts until ranking succeeds. If ranking fails, the existing list, including custom mirrors, stays unchanged.
features.recovery_includes_system_snapshots_a_boo: Recovery includes system snapshots, a boot guard, optional home-folder snapshots and factory-reset procedures. The Handbook describes supported layouts, destructive confirmations and limitations. Snapshots are not a substitute for an independent backup. Both factory resets and the boot guard’s rollback have passed on an encrypted disk in a virtual machine.
features.moonlight_sunshine_sharing_and_tailscale: Moonlight, Sunshine sharing and Tailscale away access have setup workflows and native status panels. Sharing remains inactive until explicitly configured. It controls a signed-in, awake desktop. Real-device checks are recorded, but final validation remains open; headless use, access before login and wake on LAN are future work. Stop sharing before locking when privacy matters.

development.a_terminal_environment_is_included_edito: A terminal environment is included. Editors and toolchains are yours to choose. Eitr connects the work around them: project folders, Git identities, cloud contexts and optional AI coding agents.
development.kitty_zsh_tmux_neovim_with_lazyvim_git_l: Kitty, Zsh, tmux, Neovim with LazyVim, Git, Lazygit, Lazydocker, Docker and Docker Compose are included in Eitr’s package manifest. Installing Eitr does not install every editor, language environment or coding agent.
development.what_is_there_on_day_one_and_what_you_ch: What is there on day one, and what you choose
development.use_learn_s_lazyvim_tmux_and_cmux_refere: . Use Learn’s LazyVim, tmux and cmux references without leaving the desktop.
development.official_packages_aur_builds_and_managed: . Official packages, AUR builds and managed installers keep their source-specific requirements.
development.javascript_tools_adds_pnpm_yarn_bun_and_: . JavaScript Tools adds pnpm, Yarn, Bun and Deno; Languages also offers mise for managing several runtimes.
development.development_lazyvim_projects_or_vs_code_: Development → LazyVim Projects or VS Code Projects asks for a folder, starting in your home folder, and opens it in that editor. The VS Code workflow requires VS Code to be installed.
development.installation_terminals_explain_what_is_h: Installation terminals explain what is happening and request permission where needed. Named Install lists mark installed tools; Delete offers confirmed removal. The Pacman/Yay package pickers remain install-only. Managed toolchain removal explains its wider effect before proceeding.
development.opens_walker_s_main_menu_typing_searches: opens Walker’s main menu. Typing searches apps and actions across Elephant menus; inside a submenu it searches that branch.
development.hyprland_handles_tiling_directional_focu: Hyprland handles tiling, directional focus and workspace navigation.
development.opens_control_center_graphical_configura: opens Control Center. Graphical configuration offers another entrance to the same settings and actions.
development.read_the_generated_keyboard_mouse_refere: Read the generated keyboard & mouse reference →
development.install_ai_clis_offers_claude_code_codex: Install → AI CLIs offers Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, Grok Build, Gemini CLI, Antigravity CLI, OpenCode and Pi. The packaged Eitr skill gives Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode desktop guidance without replacing user instructions. Eitr’s first-use launchers offer installation when a supported command is missing; installed binaries take precedence. No assistant binaries, credentials or subscriptions are bundled.
development.choose_a_machine_local_default_in_develo: Choose a machine-local default in Development → Default Assistant, then open it with
development.it_starts_trusted_in_your_home_folder_wi: . It starts trusted in your home folder, with full access to change files and run commands, and offline Handbook guidance where supported. Choose Settings → Security → Assistant Access → Ask before changes to restore permission prompts. Development → AI opens normal sessions in a picked folder, with per-CLI options for named, continued or resumed sessions where supported. Each cloud assistant has an Accounts submenu: add, select or delete accounts manually; running sessions keep their original account. Antigravity and OpenCode offer only Default. Pi supports accounts but cannot launch in Ask before changes mode because it has no built-in permission prompts. The bar’s AI Usage panel reports supported clients’ usage, grouped by assistant and readable account; usage a client cannot report is left out, and sections start closed at each login. Account types and API billing may differ.
development.ratatoskr_is_the_experimental_local_assi: Ratatoskr is the experimental local assistant: after one-time model downloads it runs on this PC without an account. Control Center also offers disposable, read-only quick chat with your default assistant and relevant Handbook context; closing it clears the conversation. Cloud chat sends your messages to the provider. Failed task terminals offer Ask the AI when you choose to share their output.
development.let_assistants_work_together_is_off_by_d: “Let assistants work together” is off by default. Supported, configured clients can request a second opinion through a local MCP bridge. Eitr retains the caller’s approval prompt, intends helpers for read-only consultation, and prevents onward delegation. Questions and context may go to the helper’s provider and count toward its limits.
development.availability_is_distinct_from_validation: Availability is distinct from validation. The Handbook records sign-in detection and per-client restrictions; Gemini needs an API key (a free one works) or a Google Cloud account; a read-only question and a bridge call have passed with a free key, while plan mode’s file and shell limits are not independently verified. Antigravity is available as a standalone client and is not a collaboration helper. Do not treat the bridge as a security sandbox or enable blanket tool approval for it.
development.development_git_accounts_configures_a_de: Development → Git Accounts configures a default identity and folder-specific rules after a review step. SSH keys and GitHub/GitLab CLI logins stay separate per account. Repository-local settings win; Eitr does not rewrite remotes or switch global provider CLI logins.
development.development_cloud_selects_an_account_bef: Development → Cloud selects an account before opening resource tools. AWS profiles, Google Cloud configurations/projects and Azure tenants/subscriptions remain visible. Returning from a terminal retains the context without changing global CLI defaults.
development.additional_menus_cover_cloudflare_digita: Additional menus cover Cloudflare, DigitalOcean, Hetzner Cloud, Oracle Cloud, Vercel, Netlify and IBM Cloud in private per-account workspaces. These do not import existing provider credentials. Browser consoles use their own sessions; confirm their account separately. Newer provider workflows have mock-tested views, with live sign-in and resource checks still pending.
development.cloud_operations_use_your_provider_permi: Cloud operations use your provider permissions. Some actions modify resources and can incur charges; a menu entry is not a promise of a free service or universal live testing.
development.optional_local_tools_and_your_services: Optional / Local tools and your services
development.client_installation_does_not_provision_a: . Client installation does not provision a remote database or grant access. Postman, Bruno and Insomnia are optional Developer Apps for API work.
development.development_monitoring_saves_named_dashb: Development → Monitoring saves named dashboard links for Grafana, Datadog, Sentry, New Relic, Prometheus or another service and opens them in your browser. It is a dashboard launcher, not a bundled monitoring backend. Monitoring Tools offers promtool and the Sentry CLI. Amazon Managed Grafana workspaces are under the selected AWS account.
development.accounts_service_configuration_and_permi: Accounts, service configuration and permissions remain yours. Keep passwords and tokens out of dashboard URLs and shared configuration.
development.read_the_complete_development_handbook_c: Read the complete development Handbook chapter →
development.plugins_come_from_git_repositories_inclu: Plugins come from Git repositories, including the official
development.collection_install_plugins_add_plugin_ac: collection. Install → Plugins → Add Plugin… accepts HTTPS or private SSH URLs, including repositories with several plugins. Each plugin has its own
development.manifest_and_review_two_confirmations_co: manifest and review: two confirmations cover the risks, author, exact commit and declared code before anything runs. Walker actions appear under Tools → Plugins.
development.schema_v2_adds_control_center_tiles_and_: Schema v2 adds Control Center tiles and panels, desktop widgets and bar items, with optional Eitr styling, audio spectrum levels and live data streams. Control Center → Plugins manages enable switches, details, previews and visual placements. Hooks can run on theme, wallpaper, successful System Update and login events.
development.plugins_stay_pinned_per_user_to_the_appr: Plugins stay pinned per user to the approved commit and run with your account’s full permissions. System Update only reports an available-update count. Install → Plugins → Update Plugins or Control Center → Plugins opens the separate review of commits, changed files, risk flags and diffs before approval;
development.does_the_same_from_a_terminal_eitr_has_n: does the same from a terminal. Eitr has not reviewed third-party plugin code.
development.the_same_desktop_manages_displays_sound_: The same desktop manages displays, sound, capture and appearance. System Update checks news and packages before taking a Btrfs snapshot when an upgrade is needed on supported setups. The Handbook covers recovery boundaries and independent backups.
development.inspect_git: Inspect the current Git identity and account-aware CLI

installation.the_eitr_linux_iso_includes_the_packages: The Eitr Linux ISO includes the packages for an offline guided installation. The current download is
installation.for_early_users_with_specific_tested_con: for early users, with specific tested configurations and work still open. Beta is a validation status, not a list of missing desktop or developer features.
installation.an_x86_64_pc_or_vm_booted_in_uefi_mode_a: An x86_64 PC or VM booted in UEFI mode. Apple Silicon testing uses x86_64 emulation; it is not a native ARM port.
installation.the_guided_installer_lists_writable_disk: The guided installer lists writable disks of at least 64 GiB. Erase mode removes the selected disk’s contents after confirmation.
installation.install_alongside_mode_requires_a_gpt_di: Install-alongside mode requires a GPT disk with at least 34 GiB unallocated in one gap. Prepare that space first; the installer does not resize existing partitions.
installation.the_supported_fresh_install_layout_uses_: The supported fresh-install layout uses Btrfs for Eitr’s snapshot and recovery workflows. Disk encryption (LUKS2) asks for a passphrase of at least 12 characters and unlocks in about two seconds at boot; three or four random words are strong and easy to type.
installation.no_network_is_required_for_the_guided_in: No network is required for the guided installation. Later updates, optional downloads and online services need a connection.
installation.installation_takes_about_two_minutes_in_: Installation takes about two minutes in a virtual machine on a fast computer, with nothing to download.
installation.back_up_your_files_before_changing_a_dis: Back up your files before changing a disk. Verify the ISO with its published SHA-256 checksum and read the canonical guide for the complete installation and recovery requirements.
installation.several_machines_answers_stick_organizat: Several machines / Answers stick & organization profiles
installation.to_install_without_the_wizard_format_a_u: To install without the wizard, format a USB stick as FAT32 with the label
installation.on_it_with_the_disk_layout_encryption_us: on it with the disk, layout, encryption, user, keyboard and language. The installer validates the answers like the wizard, shows what it will do and counts down 15 seconds: Ctrl+C cancels before any disk is changed. The file holds passwords in plain text; keep the stick safe and wipe it afterwards.
installation.to_the_same_stick_with_or_without_answer: to the same stick, with or without answers, for an organization profile: removed optional apps, added software, defaults and policies, all listed in Review or the countdown before the disk changes. Every referenced file must match its SHA-256 checksum first. Policies govern Eitr’s own tools; a user with root can override them. Installs with and without a network and applying a profile afterwards have passed in a virtual machine; some checks remain open.
installation.evidence_not_a_blanket_compatibility_cla: Evidence, not a blanket compatibility claim
installation.automated_offline_installation_update_an: Automated offline installation, update and factory-reset checks.
installation.installed_from_eitr_s_iso_and_used_daily: Installed from Eitr’s ISO and used daily, with updates through [eitr]. One real configuration does not establish support for every graphics card.
installation.verified_in_a_vm_with_a_simulated_window: Verified in a VM with a simulated Windows disk. Real Windows and BitLocker configurations remain to be validated.
installation.driver_handling_exists_but_broader_real_: Driver handling exists, but broader real-hardware validation remains open. Laptop power and battery features need testing on actual laptops.
installation.encrypted_installation_and_daily_use_hav: Encrypted installation and daily use have real-machine evidence. Both factory resets and the boot guard’s rollback pass on an encrypted disk in a virtual machine.
installation.eitr_detects_graphics_hardware_and_has_d: Eitr detects graphics hardware and has driver handling for AMD, Intel and NVIDIA. NVIDIA requires a reviewed driver choice because older cards need a different driver; supported Turing-or-newer systems can use the open driver. Read the guide for hybrid graphics and non-default kernels.
installation.secure_boot_setup_is_documented_in_the_h: Secure Boot setup is documented in the Handbook and is not automatically enrolled by installation. Hardware-specific boot, encryption and recovery steps deserve their own review; a successful VM installation does not verify them on your machine.
installation.a_clean_x86_64_vm_on_linux_kvm_is_the_pr: A clean x86_64 VM on Linux/KVM is the preferred first test. A Mac testing guide is also available, with the limits of emulation explained. Move to real hardware only after reviewing the guide and keeping an independent backup.
installation.on_the_desktop_system_information_report: On the desktop, Settings → System → Information → Report a Problem prepares a report for you to inspect and send. For hardware feedback, include the Eitr version, CPU/GPU, firmware mode and the exact steps and result. Remove private information before posting a public issue.

privacy.eitr_collects_no_usage_telemetry_weather: Eitr collects no usage telemetry. Weather, updates and connected tools contact their own services. Crash notifications offer help or a report for you to review and send; they are on by default and can be turned off in the Handbook welcome.
privacy.versions_of_eitr_and_its_main_packages_g: Versions of Eitr and its main packages, graphics hardware, desktop errors and warnings, recent crashes, the installation log and recent package changes. Your user name, computer name, home folder, email, IP and MAC addresses are removed before you see it. You read the whole report before sending it.
privacy.only_if_you_send_it_by_email_to_reports_: Only if you send it: by email to reports@eitr.info, or as a public GitHub issue. An email shares your email address with us; a GitHub issue is visible to everyone.
privacy.a_report_is_used_only_to_find_and_fix_th: A report is used only to find and fix the problem it describes. It is not sold, shared or used for anything else, and it is deleted once the problem is fixed.
privacy.reply_to_your_report_email_or_write_to_c: Reply to your report email, or write to contact@eitr.info, to have your report deleted at any time. You can turn crash offers off in the welcome chapter of the Handbook. Optional cloud assistants receive messages and context you share; Control Center quick chat is read-only and keeps its conversation only in memory until closed.
privacy.the_site_sets_no_cookies_iso_download_st: The site sets no cookies. ISO download starts are counted by UTC day and filename without storing visitor data; the website displays the aggregate total. Your day/night and language preferences are saved only in this browser’s local storage. It is served by Cloudflare, which processes visitors' network addresses to deliver and protect it.
privacy.collects_no_usage_telemetry_a_problem_re: collects no usage telemetry. A problem report leaves your computer only when you send it.
